newsitem.title: USA: Weekend rains halt Oklahoma fieldwork activities.
newsitem.headline: Weekend rains halt Oklahoma fieldwork activities.

text.p: Oklahoma fieldwork ground to a halt after many areas of the state received heavy rains toward the end of the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said.

Wheat seeding progressed but still lagged average levels. Wheat was ten percent seeded versus 12 percent last year and the 20-percent average. In several areas, worm infestations were already reported on early emerged small grains.
Peanut digging began in south central Oklahoma but was halted by the weekend storms. Corn, soybean and sorghum harvest "made good progress as the weather permitted."

Corn was 29 percent harvested versus 30 a year ago and 47 percent average. Sixty-one percent was mature vs 73 a year ago and 86 percent average. The corn crop was rated 88 percent good to excellent, 10 fair and 2 percent poor.
Sorghum harvest was six percent complete versus three a year ago and four percent average. The crop was 26 percent mature versus 12 a year ago and 18 average.

Soybeans were 11 percent harvested versus nine a year ago and nine percent average. Soybeans were 44 percent mature vs 29 a year ago and 32 average. Beans were rated 67 pct good to excellent, 26 fair, 7 poor.
Cotton bolls were 25 percent opening vs seven a year ago and 24 average. Cotton was rated 49 percent good to excellent, 31 fair, 20 poor to very poor.
Pasture and range conditions were rated 84 percent good to excellent versus 74 percent at that level last week.
